observations: Photo 0 shows a black UPS unit with 'BLUE GATE' embossed on the front panel. A blue vertical strip with a power button and three indicator lights (green, amber, red) is visible. The unit appears to be on a tiled floor.
Photo 1 shows the same UPS from a side angle, with the top plug visible. The unit has ventilation grilles on the sides. The power cord is connected to the top plug.
The unit has a matte black finish with some minor scuffs and dust. The indicator lights are not illuminated in either photo.
No model number or serial number is visible in either photo.
The seller claims it is an UPS, which is consistent with the visible unit type.

claims.evidence: The photos show a UPS unit with the brand 'BLUE GATE' visible on the front panel. The unit appears to be a standard UPS design with power input and indicator lights.

risks.risk: The UPS may not be functional or may have internal damage not visible in photos.
risks.proof: A video showing the UPS powering on, the indicator lights turning on, and the unit maintaining power during a simulated load.

risks.risk: The unit may be missing essential components such as the battery, charger, or manual.
risks.proof: A photo showing the battery compartment open or a close-up of the battery and charger.

risks.risk: The model number is not visible, which affects pricing and compatibility.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the model label, usually on the back or bottom of the unit.
risks.if_unproven: priced at the lowest common model in the brand

proof_requests: A clear photo of the model label on the back or bottom of the UPS.
A video showing the UPS powering on and maintaining power during a load.
A photo of the battery and charger if included.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
